row.notes: (obj, u8 carIdx) -> const char *, the driver name of a car. 0xff, or an index at or past the count of the car pointer vector [obj+0x88, obj+0x90), returns "" (0x145612762). The car is cached at obj+0xa0+idx*8 (read 0x142f28c4a); on a miss the vector is searched for the car whose [[car+0x18]+0x58] byte +0xe8 equals the index (a null link gives 0xff) and the hit is cached (0x142f28cf5). A car whose byte +0x32 has the sign bit set returns the shared qword [obj+0x60] (0x142f28d08). Any other car takes its 0x88-byte record from [[[obj+0x190]+0x88]+0x260]+0x2e0..+0x2e8 where byte +0x82 equals the index, looks the driver up by the stat id at record+0x50 through 0x1423dbcf0([obj+0x198], &record[0x50]) (it returns 0 when it finds none, logging ENTRANTS_SYSTEM 'Driver with stat id %s not found' when the stat id's type is past 2 or its table is missing) and returns qword [driver+0xc8] (0x142f28d36); a null [[obj+0x190]+0x88] or [[[obj+0x190]+0x88]+0x260], no matching record or no driver returns "", while [obj+0x190] and [obj+0x198] themselves are read with no null check. Neither [obj+0x60] nor [driver+0xc8] is null-checked, so the result can be NULL. Callers: Sess_Misconduct_OnCarToCarCollision, Sess_PenaltyLog_Print, Sess_Misconduct_RemoveWatchedIncident, 0x1435b3550 (the unlapped rules message) and .data1 0x15026e7b0. Callers: census steam 0x2f28c10.
